title: Body scan
intro: A slow tour through the body to settle a restless mind.

blocks.text: Find a comfortable position, sitting or lying down. Let your eyes close, or soften your gaze downward.
Take three slow breaths. With each out-breath, let your body get a little heavier.
Bring your attention to the top of your head. Just notice any sensation there — warmth, tingling, or nothing at all.
Slowly move your attention down — your face, your jaw. Let your jaw unclench.
Down through your shoulders and arms, all the way to your fingertips. There's nothing to fix. Only notice.
Into your chest and stomach, rising and falling with the breath.
Down through your hips, your legs, to the soles of your feet. Notice the whole body, held by the floor.
Rest here for a moment as a whole. When you're ready, open your eyes and carry this steadiness with you.

title: Loving-kindness
intro: Warm wishes for yourself and others — an antidote to shame.

blocks.text: Settle comfortably and take a few easy breaths. Place a hand on your heart if that feels okay.
Silently offer these words to yourself: May I be safe. May I be well. May I be at peace.
Notice how it feels to wish yourself well — even if part of you resists. Let that be okay.
Now picture someone you care about. Offer them the same: May you be safe. May you be well. May you be at peace.
Widen it to someone you find difficult, then to all people trying, like you, to be well.
Return to yourself once more: May I be kind to myself, especially when I struggle. Rest here a moment before you finish.

title: Self-compassion break
intro: Three steps to meet a hard moment with kindness.

blocks.text: Bring to mind something that's weighing on you right now. Feel where it sits in your body.
First, acknowledge it: "This is a moment of struggle." Naming pain is not weakness — it's honesty.
Second, remember you're not alone: "Struggle is part of being human. Others feel this too."
Third, offer yourself kindness. Place a hand on your heart and say: "May I be gentle with myself right now."
You'd offer this to a friend without hesitation. You're allowed to offer it to yourself. Take one more slow breath and return.

title: Muscle relaxation
intro: Tense and release each muscle group to drain physical anxiety.

blocks.text: Sit or lie down somewhere you won't be disturbed. We'll gently tense, then release, each part of the body.
Start with your hands. Clench both fists tight for five seconds… and let go. Notice the difference.
Now your arms — tense them toward your shoulders… hold… and release.
Your shoulders — lift them up toward your ears… hold… and let them drop.
Your face — scrunch it tight… hold… and soften everything.
Your stomach — tighten the muscles… hold… and release.
Your legs — press your feet into the floor and tense… hold… and let go.
Now let your whole body be loose and heavy. Notice the calm that follows tension leaving. Rest here, then finish when ready.

title: One small step
intro: A short practice to move from stuck toward one doable action.

blocks.text: Low mood makes everything feel heavy and pointless. We're not going to fight that feeling — just take one tiny step alongside it.
Take a slow breath. Notice you showed up here. That already counts.
Think of one small thing that once gave you a flicker of pleasure or accomplishment. Small is good — the smaller the better.
Picture yourself doing just the first 10 minutes of it. Not the whole thing. Just the start.
Notice your mood right now, 0 to 10. Hold that number lightly.
When this ends, go do that first small step — before you feel ready. Then check your mood again. Let the evidence, not the whisper, decide what's true.

title: Wind down for sleep
intro: A calming practice to help your body shift toward rest.

blocks.text: Lie down comfortably. This is the end of the day — nothing left to do but rest.
Breathe in for a count of four… and out for a count of six. The long out-breath tells your body it's safe to slow down.
Let the day go. If thoughts about tomorrow arrive, imagine setting them on a shelf — they'll be there in the morning.
Feel the weight of your body sinking into the bed, fully supported.
Soften your face, your shoulders, your hands. Let each breath out release a little more.
There's nothing to achieve here — not even sleep. Just rest. Let the breath carry you gently down.
